title: Adverbs of manner (-ment)
goal: By the end of this lesson you can form adverbs ending in -ment from adjectives, handle the -amment / -emment forms and the irregular ones, and place adverbs correctly in the present and the passé composé.

body: Most adverbs of manner are made from the **feminine** form of the adjective + **-ment** (like English -ly): *lent → lente → lentement* (slowly), *heureux → heureuse → heureusement* (luckily).
Adverbs never agree: *Elle parle lentement. Ils parlent lentement.*
If the masculine adjective ends in a vowel (*-é, -i, -u, -ai*), add *-ment* to the **masculine**: *vrai → vraiment*, *poli → poliment*, *absolu → absolument*, *spontané → spontanément*.

Adjectives ending in *-ant* become *-amment*, and those in *-ent* become *-emment*: *courant → couramment*, *constant → constamment*, *évident → évidemment*, *récent → récemment*, *patient → patiemment*.
Both endings are pronounced the same way: **[a-mahn]**. *Évidemment* = [é-vi-da-mahn].
Some adverbs take an *é* before *-ment*: *précis → précisément*, *énorme → énormément*, *profond → profondément*. A few are irregular: *gentil → gentiment*, *bref → brièvement*.
The most common adverbs of manner are not in *-ment* at all: *bien* (well), *mal* (badly), *vite* (fast), *mieux* (better). Note: *bon → bien*, *mauvais → mal*, *rapide → rapidement* or *vite*.
In simple tenses, the adverb goes **after the verb**: *Il conduit* **prudemment**. *Je parle* **lentement**.

In the passé composé, short common adverbs go **between** the auxiliary and the participle: *J'ai* **bien** *dormi*. *Tu as* **vite** *compris*. *Il a* **mal** *fait ça*. Longer *-ment* adverbs usually go after the participle: *Il a répondu* **poliment**, though some (*vraiment, complètement, déjà*) go between: *J'ai complètement oublié!*
Sentence adverbs (*heureusement, malheureusement, finalement*) often start the sentence: *Heureusement, il ne pleuvait pas.*

examples.fr: Parle plus lentement, s'il te plaît.
Il conduit prudemment sur la glace.
examples.en: He drives carefully on the ice.

examples.fr: Heureusement, l'autobus est arrivé à l'heure.
examples.en: Luckily, the bus arrived on time.

examples.fr: Il a répondu poliment à la cliente.
On a bien mangé et bien dormi.
examples.en: We ate well and slept well.
examples.note: short adverbs between avoir and the participle
patient → patiemment; ça s'en vient is common in Quebec

examples.fr: C'est exactement ce que je voulais.
Il a énormément neigé cette nuit.
Ferme la porte doucement, le bébé dort.
examples.en: Close the door gently, the baby's sleeping.

quebec.intro: In Quebec speech, 'bien' is very often pronounced 'ben', and it's used everywhere as an intensifier: 'ben correct' (totally fine), 'ben bon' (really good). 'Pas ben ben' means 'not very much'. The expression 'tranquillement pas vite' means 'slowly but surely'.

items.note: ben = bien; correct = OK, fine; informal

items.en: I don't like that very much.
items.note: pas ben ben = not very much; informal

items.en: It's moving along slowly but surely.

items.note: very common; ben non = of course not

drills.why: Ends in a vowel: masculine + ment.
Short adverbs go between avoir and the participle: j'ai bien dormi.

drills.en: Drive carefully, the road is slippery.
drills.a: Conduis prudemment, la route est glissante.

a: Parle plus lentement, s'il te plaît.
Parlez plus lentement, s'il vous plaît.

pron.tip: lahnt-MAHN: the middle e is dropped.

dialogue.en: OK, let's start. Start up gently.

dialogue.fr: Parfait. Maintenant, avance lentement. La route est glissante.
dialogue.en: Perfect. Now, move forward slowly. The road is slippery.

dialogue.fr: Oui, c'est ben correct. Regarde attentivement à gauche avant de tourner.
dialogue.en: Yes, that's totally fine. Look carefully to the left before turning.

dialogue.fr: Oups! J'ai complètement oublié mon clignotant!
dialogue.en: Oops! I completely forgot my turn signal!

dialogue.fr: Heureusement, il n'y avait personne. Mets-le toujours, d'accord?
dialogue.en: Luckily, there was nobody there. Always put it on, OK?

dialogue.fr: Évidemment. Ça avance tranquillement pas vite, hein?
dialogue.en: Of course. It's coming along slowly but surely, eh?

questions.q: Why was the mistake not serious?

speak.prompt: Describe how you do 4 things using adverbs: drive, speak French, eat, sleep.
speak.model: Je conduis prudemment. Je parle français lentement, mais correctement. Je mange rapidement le midi. Je dors bien la fin de semaine.

speak.prompt: Tell a short story with heureusement, malheureusement and finalement.
speak.model: Hier, j'ai raté l'autobus. Malheureusement, il faisait très froid. Heureusement, un ami est passé en voiture. Finalement, je suis arrivé à l'heure.

speak.prompt: Someone apologises for being a bit late. Reassure them, Quebec style.

write.prompt: Write 5–6 sentences about your progress in French. Use at least six different adverbs, including one in -amment or -emment and one in the passé composé.
write.model: J'apprends le français régulièrement depuis un an. Au début, je parlais très lentement. Récemment, j'ai beaucoup progressé. Maintenant, je comprends facilement les conversations simples. Malheureusement, je ne parle pas encore couramment. Mais ça avance tranquillement pas vite!

quiz.why: Ends in a vowel: absolu + ment.
Short adverb between avoir and the participle.

options: I don't like that very much
quiz.why: Pas ben ben = not very much.
